letter:
Dear Example Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Junior Software Engineer position. My experience building tested Node.js services, accessible booking workflows, and a React-based scheduling project aligns closely with the practical focus of this role. I am particularly interested in work where reliable APIs and clear user interactions are treated as equally important parts of the product.

During my Software Engineering Internship at Example Studio, I built appointment-conflict validation in a Node.js API and added regression tests for overlapping bookings. That work required translating a user-facing scheduling rule into backend validation and protecting the behavior with automated tests. I also replaced an inaccessible date picker with a keyboard-operated booking flow, testing the revised interaction with the product team. This strengthened my interest in accessibility as a core engineering concern rather than a final-stage adjustment.

I have continued developing these skills through Booking Lab, an independent appointment scheduler built with TypeScript, React, Node.js, and PostgreSQL. The project includes persistent storage and automated conflict tests. I documented the tradeoff between enforcing booking rules through database constraints and handling them in application validation, then created a reproducible local demo. This work reflects how I approach engineering decisions: make the behavior testable, explain the tradeoffs clearly, and leave the project straightforward for another developer to run.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute this foundation in API testing, React development, and accessible workflows to Example Hiring Team. While my current record does not include Kubernetes operations, I am interested in expanding my infrastructure knowledge alongside the team. Thank you for considering my application. I would be glad to discuss how my experience and ongoing Computer Science studies could support the role.

Sincerely,
Zoë Șerban
